title: Feature file v2.2.0
description: `features/<name>/feature.json`: the committed assignment `workflow launch <name>` prepares. `workers` declares every lane: a node id that must match a `workers[].node_id` of the policy file and the task file that lane receives. `launch --workers a,b` selects a subset; omitted means every declared lane. 2.1.0 adds the optional `reviewers`: every reviewer of the run with its brief (a file relative to the feature directory, existing and non-empty, or `builtin:<id>` for a brief bundled in `workflow/prompts/reviewers/`); a file without `reviewers` runs the single built-in reviewer (`workflow/prompts/review.md`) with id `review`. A 1.0.0 file (`ui_task`/`adapter_task`) is refused by `launch` with a message to use 2.x. Hand-written; the controller validates it with `workflow.verification.validate_schema("feature", ...)` and additionally requires unique node ids, the same id set as the policy, existing non-empty task and brief files inside the feature directory, unique reviewer ids that are neither a lane id nor a reserved name, and version 2.1.0 or later whenever `reviewers` is present. 2.2.0 turns on the guardrails (docs/PRD_PORTABLE_WORKFLOW.md section 4.3): every task must have non-empty `## Goal`, `## Acceptance` and `## Stop` sections, the feature directory must hold a non-empty `decisions.md`, and `prd` must exist in the target; it adds the optional `challenge` (default true: a design challenge runs before any worker) and `prd`. 2.0.0 and 2.1.0 files launch as before, with a note that no guardrail is enforced.

policy.description: Policy file relative to the feature directory (contracts/workflow/verification.schema.json).

node_id.description: A lane id as the policy declares it: lower-case, at most 32 characters, never a reserved graph name, attribution or per-lane prefix.

task.description: Task file relative to the feature directory.

reviewers.description: 2.1.0: the reviewers the review node launches in parallel over the same candidate, in declared order. Each reviewer owns the node `review-<reviewer_id>` and the files `review-<reviewer_id>.*`.

reviewer_id.description: Lower-case, at most 32 characters, unique, never a lane id of the policy nor a reserved graph name, attribution or per-lane prefix.

prompt.description: Brief file relative to the feature directory, or `builtin:<id>` for a bundled brief (workflow/prompts/reviewers/<id>.md); it replaces the built-in brief and states only what to look for (the controller appends the bundle paths, task locations, lane vocabulary and completion protocol).

challenge.description: 2.2.0: run the design challenge node before any worker launch (default true). `false` records the challenge as disabled and the run's graph has no challenge node.

prd.description: 2.2.0: the specification the design challenge reads, a path relative to the target repository that must exist.
